Beside the anvil sits a fat bag of patched, stitched animal skin with a wooden nozzle, clearly bigger than the anvil and bigger than the shed, taut and rounded like a squat pear, tied with rope. Scrap wood, rope, sewn patches. A stocky young apprentice in a plain tunic and a soft cap pushes down on the skin bag with both hands, arms straight, doing a push-up on it. Matte iron, matte dull, no shine. A small feathered patch of ground under it, no hard-edged slab. Three-quarter view from above, no front view, no hanging cloth, no smoke clutter.
